+The presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) is not \emph{a priori} a sheaf (Kleiman
+\S 2, L1330), and over a general field it is not representable: by Kleiman's
+Exercise \texttt{ex:Pfs}, the conic \(u^2+v^2+w^2=0\) in \(\I P^2_\bb R\) --- a
+smooth plane conic, hence smooth, proper and geometrically integral, over a field
+where it has no rational point --- carries a class of
+\(\Pic_{(X/\bb R)\et}(\bb R)\) outside the image of
+\(\Pic_{(X/\bb R)\zar}(\bb R)\), so \(\Pic_{X/\bb R}\) is not representable while
+\(\Pic_{(X/\bb R)\et}\) is.
+
+\emph{Citation corrected} (2026-07-29, \texttt{review-ajc}). This passage
+previously attributed the obstruction to Kleiman \S 2, L1292--L1302, glossed as:
+for a \(T\) carrying a non-trivial line bundle whose pullback becomes trivial on
+an open cover, the Zariski separated-presheaf condition fails. That argument is
+Kleiman's, but it is about the \emph{absolute} functor \(\Pic_X\); the quotient by
+\(\Pic(T)\) defining the relative functor is exactly what defeats it, and
+L1600--L1605 proves \(\Pic_{X/S} \risom \Pic_{(X/S)\zar}\) when \(f\) has a
+section. The conclusion is unchanged; only its stated reason was wrong.
+
